title: Treasury Repurchase Agreement Risk Management

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The Treasury Market Practices Group (TMPG) issued FAQs on best practice recommendations for U.S. Treasury repo risk management, recommending that all Treasury repos include haircuts or margin and other risk management techniques. The guidance identifies systemic risks from inconsistent risk management practices in the bilateral repo market and calls for legally enforceable documentation of margining regimes. Implementation is recommended by June 2026.
key_points: TMPG recommends applying haircuts or margin on all Treasury repurchase agreements, reflecting counterparty credit risk, liquidity risk, and market risk
Bilateral repo market lacks consistency and transparency in risk management practices, potentially creating unknown leverage in the system
Large quantities of repos without prudent risk management could pose systemic risks to market functioning if a participant defaults
Working group convened in February 2023 included dealers, money funds, hedge funds, asset managers, financial market utilities, clearing banks, and Federal Reserve staff
Recommended implementation deadline is June 2026 with a risk-based rolling approach prioritizing material counterparty exposures
Centrally cleared repo already adheres to the recommended best practice through CCP margining regimes
why_it_matters: This guidance addresses potential systemic vulnerabilities in the Treasury repo market. Inconsistent risk management in bilateral repos could amplify market stress during periods of volatility. The recommended implementation of haircuts and robust documentation frameworks aims to reduce counterparty exposure and prevent cascading defaults. Market participants using bilateral (non-centrally-cleared) repo must review and update their legal agreements and risk frameworks before the June 2026 deadline.
market_structure_context: The FAQ addresses non-centrally cleared bilateral repo (NCCBR) market risk management practices, documents requirements for legally enforceable margining agreements, and acknowledges that not all repo transactions will likely be eligible for central clearing as SEC's mandatory central clearing rule amendments are implemented. The guidance is intended to complement central clearing expansion rather than replace it.
